status: development protocol recorded before implementation; not independent preregistration
question: Does a proposed decision-boundary abstraction improve on an ordinary explicit encoding for the declared cancellation/command fragment?
arms: Explicit operational reference with cancellation counter, cleanup outcome, patch state, and command cursor
Conventional version-dispatch harness executing the actual B/C/V helper AST against declared primitive adapters
Reduced decision-boundary formula with a separately computed observation map
primitive_contract: Caller exists. Prefix events occur while the helper awaits child cleanup. cancel increments the caller counter; uncancel decrements it with floor zero.
The child settles with the selected outcome after the finite prefix. Child cancellation and caller cancellation are separate inputs.

No later suspension or cancellation occurs between helper return and the final gate/dispatch decision. Gate outcome is a fixed input; publication and argument preparation are total and command-free in this fragment.

Reached patch calls use the existing memo when present. Otherwise replay uses notification; fresh execution uses the activation input. A newly true result emits one patch symbol, while memo reuse emits none.
Activity name/argument/options are represented by one opaque signature. This symbol records an API command request, not a durable external effect.
Expected-word comparison is exact ordered symbolic equality, with an explicit reference cursor. It is NOT Temporal core replay matching or a claim about real history reachability.

predictions.claim: All three encodings agree on supported terminal outcome, patch-call reachability, and command word.
A cancellation Boolean maintained throughout the prefix is insufficient when uncancel is allowed: cancel,uncancel and cancel,cancel,uncancel are a distinguishing pair.
At the post-cleanup decision boundary, count positivity suffices for this suffix under the declared no-later-cancellation restriction.
Assuming every fresh reached patch activates gives a wrong answer when activation is disabled.
An unconditional patch call changes observable behavior when the cancellation counter is zero.
Comparing command kind alone falsely accepts changes to activity arguments/options.
The conventional encoding can express the supported cases; no expressiveness advantage is expected.

scoring: Report complete Cartesian domain size, every disagreement, deterministic transcript hash, and all unsupported probes.
Report conditional cancellation-policy violations separately from agreement: accurate prediction of unsafe baseline behavior is not safety certification.
Count distinct explicit decision-boundary keys and reduced keys with identical external context; do not interpret enumeration-size reduction as runtime speedup.
Record hand-authored semantic contracts and source-derived pieces. No manual-effort superiority claim without independently measured effort.
Any supported disagreement falsifies the reduction or an implementation; retain the failure and protocol version before fixing.
If the conventional encoding agrees at this scope, do not claim novelty from the reduced formula or this experiment.
